paragraphs: The paper asks whether transformers learning from natural language show a simplicity bias: a tendency to learn simpler patterns before more complicated ones. This idea has helped explain generalization in supervised feed-forward networks, but its relevance to transformers trained through self-supervision has been less clear. Here, simplicity is examined through relationships among input tokens.

The researchers develop a procedure for generating controlled versions, called clones, of a natural-language dataset. Each clone rigorously captures token interactions up to a specified order. This creates a way to study the contribution of interactions involving different numbers of tokens, rather than treating all statistical structure in language as a single undifferentiated source of learning.

Their analysis finds that transformers learn these interactions sequentially. Prediction error associated with lower-order interactions reaches a plateau while learning of higher-order interactions continues. This supports a distributional form of simplicity bias in the studied setting. The cloning procedure also offers a means of investigating how interaction order affects learning beyond this particular language-model analysis.
neurips-2024-a-distributional-simplicity.tldr: Controlled versions of language datasets reveal that transformers learn lower-order token interactions before continuing to learn higher-order ones.

paragraphs: BioMed-VITAL addresses how to adapt general multimodal models to biomedical tasks using instruction data that reflects clinical expertise. Automatically generated medical training examples can provide scale, but their generation alone does not explicitly align them with clinician preferences. The paper makes those preferences part of both producing candidate examples and deciding which examples enter training.

During generation, GPT-4V receives a diverse collection of demonstrations selected by clinicians. These demonstrations guide the creation of candidate instruction data. During selection, a separate model learns a rating function from clinician preferences and preferences supplied by a policy-guided model. That function then selects high-quality examples for tuning the biomedical multimodal model.

The resulting instruction data improves the evaluated model's performance on open visual chat and medical visual question answering. The abstract reports an 18.5% relative improvement in open visual chat and a medical question-answering win rate reaching 81.73%. These findings support the value of incorporating domain preferences into the construction of training data, with guidance operating at two distinct stages.
neurips-2024-biomedical-visual-instructi.tldr: BioMed-VITAL uses clinician preferences to generate and select instruction data, improving evaluated biomedical visual conversations and question answering.

paragraphs: Brain Treebank connects detailed language annotations with electrical brain recordings collected while people watched Hollywood movies. Ten subjects contributed 43 hours of viewing in total, averaging 4.3 hours and 2.6 movies each. Because the language occurs within movies, the recordings capture responses to speech embedded in visual and narrative context.

The researchers transcribed movie audio and manually corrected the transcripts. They also manually marked word onset times using audio spectrograms. Each transcript received a syntactic analysis in the universal dependencies format, with a part-of-speech label for every word and grammatical dependency relationships for every sentence. Automatic parses were manually corrected, linking structured linguistic descriptions to precisely timed stimuli.

Across the recordings, subjects heard more than 38,000 sentences and 223,000 words, with an average of 168 implanted electrodes per subject. The paper also analyzes which electrodes respond to language features and sketches the timing of processing across them. The dataset is intended to connect linguistic structure, perception, and neural representations through aligned observations.
neurips-2024-brain-treebank-large-scale-.tldr: Brain Treebank aligns movie dialogue and grammatical annotations with 43 hours of intracranial recordings from ten subjects.

paragraphs: SuperClass explores a simple way to learn visual representations from paired images and text: use classification as the training task. In the comparison described by the paper, CLIP learns through a contrastive target supplied by a text encoder. SuperClass instead treats tokens from the raw accompanying text as supervised classification labels.

This choice changes what the training system needs to maintain. The method does not require a text encoder, additional filtering or selection of the text, or the large batch sizes associated with CLIP's contrastive training. Text still provides the supervision, but it enters through classification labels rather than through a separately encoded contrastive target.

The paper reports superior performance on a range of downstream tasks covering both conventional computer vision benchmarks and vision-language applications. It also investigates changes in model size, training duration, and dataset size, reporting encouraging scaling results and comparisons with CLIP. Together, these findings suggest that this simpler use of image-text supervision can produce useful representations across the evaluated tasks and scales.
neurips-2024-classification-done-right-f.tldr: SuperClass trains on image-text pairs by using text tokens as classification labels, removing the text encoder and large-batch requirement of CLIP-style training.

paragraphs: Convolutional layers are intuitive, but their detailed mathematical structure can make them harder to analyze than dense layers. This complicates adapting theoretical results and optimization methods to convolutions. The paper introduces a tensor-network view that expresses the underlying tensor multiplications through diagrams and evaluates them efficiently with einsum operations.

These diagrams can be manipulated to perform transformations such as differentiation. The authors derive representations for automatic-differentiation operations and commonly used curvature approximations, supporting convolution hyperparameters, batches, channel groups, and arbitrary convolution dimensions. They also introduce simplifications based on the connectivity pattern of convolutions, allowing a computation's diagram to be reduced before it is evaluated.

The paper tests whether this representation brings practical computational benefits. Its implementation speeds up a recently proposed KFAC variant by as much as 4.5 times while removing the standard implementation's memory overhead. It also enables hardware-efficient tensor dropout for approximate backpropagation. The contribution therefore combines a framework for reasoning about convolutions with demonstrated improvements for particular derivative and curvature computations.
neurips-2024-convolutions-and-more-as-ei.tldr: A tensor-network formulation makes convolutional computations easier to manipulate and accelerates an evaluated KFAC variant by up to 4.5 times.

paragraphs: COVE tackles temporal consistency when using a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model to edit video. Such models can edit individual images, but their ordinary formulation lacks constraints connecting successive frames. The paper uses correspondences already present in diffusion features to connect related content across a video's frames during editing.

A sliding-window procedure compares feature tokens from the source video and identifies strongly corresponding tokens across frames. During inversion and denoising, COVE uses these correspondences to sample tokens from the noisy latent representation and perform self-attention among them. This gives the editing process a way to coordinate content associated with matching parts of different frames.

The method also merges tokens along the temporal dimension to reduce redundant computation, lower GPU memory use, and accelerate editing. It integrates with pretrained text-to-image diffusion models without additional training or optimization. Across the evaluated editing scenarios, the authors report state-of-the-art results in both quantitative and qualitative comparisons, supporting correspondence-guided attention as a practical mechanism for improving consistency.
neurips-2024-cove-unleashing-the-diffusi.tldr: COVE uses diffusion-feature correspondences across frames to improve video-editing consistency without extra training or optimization.

paragraphs: The paper studies how to discover interpretable models of systems that change over time, focusing on drug dynamics. Such models matter because understanding a drug's behavior can inform efforts to improve treatment effectiveness and reduce harm. Expert-built models can be costly to develop, difficult to scale, and bounded by the knowledge their designers already possess.

The proposed Data-Driven Discovery framework, D3, uses a large language model in an iterative modeling process. The model can propose, acquire, and incorporate new features, then validate and compare candidate descriptions of the dynamical system. This makes the language model part of a cycle of proposing and refining interpretable models using data.

Experiments on a Warfarin pharmacokinetic dataset identify a new model that the authors describe as plausible and well-fitting. That result provides evidence for the framework's ability to discover useful candidate descriptions of drug dynamics. Its relevance to precision dosing is presented as potential for clinical applications; the stated finding concerns the discovered model and its fit to the dataset.
neurips-2024-data-driven-discovery-of-dy.tldr: D3 uses language models to iteratively discover interpretable dynamical models, finding a plausible, well-fitting candidate on a Warfarin dataset.

paragraphs: DreamScene4D generates dynamic three-dimensional scenes containing multiple objects from videos recorded from a single viewpoint. The paper identifies two obstacles: rendering-error gradients often struggle to recover rapid object motion, and models that predict new views work better for individual objects than for complete scenes. These obstacles make direct scene-level generation difficult.

Its central approach separates the video into a background and object tracks, then recombines the recovered components. Object motion is further divided into deformation within the object, movement relative to the world, and camera motion. Rendering feedback and object-oriented view-prediction models recover object shape completions and deformation, while bounding-box tracks guide larger movements through the scene.

This decomposition supports synthesis of views around the resulting scene through 360 degrees. The authors present results on DAVIS, Kubric, and self-recorded videos, including quantitative comparisons and a user preference study. The inferred three-dimensional trajectories also produce accurate persistent two-dimensional point tracks when projected back into the image, connecting scene generation with tracking over time.
neurips-2024-dreamscene4d-dynamic-multi-.tldr: DreamScene4D separates objects, background, and motion components to generate dynamic multi-object 3D scenes from monocular videos.

paragraphs: Remote photoplethysmography estimates blood-volume pulse signals from images, converting information distributed across space and time into a time series. Attention mechanisms help extract the relevant features, but existing approaches compute attention separately across spatial, temporal, and channel dimensions. This paper investigates a mechanism that considers those dimensions jointly.

The proposed Factorized Self-Attention Module, FSAM, applies nonnegative matrix factorization to voxel embeddings. The resulting factorization supplies attention spanning spatial positions, time, and feature channels. The authors build FactorizePhys, an end-to-end three-dimensional convolutional network that uses this module to estimate pulse signals directly from video frames. They also insert FSAM into an existing two-dimensional convolutional architecture to examine its versatility.

Evaluation covers four public datasets and comparisons with methods using different architectures and attention mechanisms. Ablation studies examine design choices and hyperparameters, while visualizations inspect learned space-time features. The reported results support FSAM's effectiveness and improved generalization across datasets for pulse estimation, with broader use as a multidimensional attention mechanism presented as a possibility.
neurips-2024-factorizephys-matrix-factor.tldr: FactorizePhys uses matrix factorization to compute joint spatial, temporal, and channel attention for estimating blood-volume pulse signals from video.

paragraphs: TracksTo4D reconstructs changing three-dimensional structure and camera positions from casual videos containing moving content. The paper targets the expense of approaches that need lengthy optimization and the difficulty of applying some existing methods to footage from ordinary cameras. Its reconstruction stage uses a single feed-forward pass through a learned model.

The model operates on two-dimensional point tracks extracted from video. Its architecture accounts for symmetries in this input and assumes that motion patterns can be represented effectively with a low-rank approximation. That assumption provides structure for interpreting the observed tracks. Training uses only tracks from casual videos, without three-dimensional supervision.

The output is a temporal point cloud together with camera positions. Experiments report reconstruction accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods while reducing runtime by up to 95%. The authors also find good generalization to previously unseen videos from unseen semantic categories. These findings support point-track processing as an efficient route to the evaluated dynamic reconstruction tasks, under the architecture's stated motion representation.
neurips-2024-fast-encoder-based-3d-from-.tldr: TracksTo4D learns from 2D point tracks to reconstruct dynamic 3D structure and cameras in one pass, with reported runtime reductions up to 95%.

paragraphs: This paper studies convex learning when privacy must cover each user's entire collection of data. With n users holding m items each, protecting a user means protecting all m items together. Existing algorithms can require restrictive smoothness assumptions, a number of users that grows polynomially with parameter dimension, or prohibitively many gradient computations.

The authors provide three algorithms with different computational and smoothness guarantees. The first runs in linear time under a mild smoothness assumption and achieves state-of-the-art excess risk for a nontrivial linear-time algorithm. The second handles arbitrary smooth losses and achieves optimal excess risk with approximately (mn)^(9/8) gradient computations. The third handles nonsmooth losses with optimal excess risk using n^(11/8) m^(5/4) gradient computations.

These results improve the stated computational requirements while maintaining strong guarantees on excess risk, the gap from the best achievable objective value. None of the proposed algorithms requires the user count to grow polynomially with dimension. The distinctions among their assumptions matter: the linear-time result carries a mild smoothness condition, while the other algorithms address broader loss classes.
neurips-2024-faster-algorithms-for-user-.tldr: New user-level private convex optimization algorithms reduce computation while retaining strong excess-risk guarantees under their respective smoothness conditions.

paragraphs: Identify Then Recommend, or ITR, addresses recommendation for groups whose structure is not known in advance. Existing approaches can assume a fixed number of groups and require labels connecting users to groups and groups to items. Those requirements are costly and can be awkward when the distribution of groups changes in an industrial recommendation system.

ITR first identifies groups without supervision or a predefined group count. It estimates an adaptive density around each user representation, treating denser regions as more likely group centers. A heuristic process then merges and splits groups to determine their membership and boundaries. After identification, two self-supervised tasks provide training signals: one adjusts the user-group distribution through attraction and repulsion, and another supplies pseudo group recommendations.

Experiments report improvements in both individual and group recommendation, with example NDCG@5 gains of 22.22% and 22.95%, respectively. The authors also report promising results after deployment in an industrial recommender. The approach links flexible group discovery with recommendation training that avoids the stated expensive group-level labels.
neurips-2024-identify-then-recommend-tow.tldr: ITR discovers user groups without a preset group count and trains recommendations through self-supervised tasks.

paragraphs: ImageNet3D targets visual understanding that combines recognizing an object with estimating its three-dimensional properties from an ordinary image. A central challenge is extending this ability to rigid objects from categories a model has not previously encountered. Existing datasets can restrict progress through limited category coverage or inadequate annotations, encouraging models specialized to particular objects or domains.

The dataset adds annotations to 200 ImageNet categories. These include two-dimensional bounding boxes, three-dimensional pose and location, and captions interleaved with three-dimensional information. Together, these annotations support examining what visual foundation models already know about object geometry and developing models that infer both image-level and spatial information.

The paper introduces tasks for probing object-level 3D awareness and estimating pose with an open vocabulary, alongside standard classification and pose estimation. It also identifies integration with language models for 3D reasoning as a use of the dataset. Experimental results demonstrate the dataset's potential to support stronger general-purpose understanding; the broader goal remains inference across arbitrary rigid objects in natural images.
neurips-2024-imagenet3d-towards-general-.tldr: ImageNet3D adds spatial annotations to 200 ImageNet categories to support broader object-level 3D understanding and evaluation.

paragraphs: This paper examines why gradient-based adversarial prompt generation can struggle even when an attacker has access to a language model's internals. Text changes through discrete token replacements, while gradients describe local changes in a continuous representation. Consequently, a gradient may poorly predict how replacing a token will affect the attack's objective.

The authors adapt ideas from two methods originally developed for transfer-based attacks on image classifiers: Skip Gradient Method and Intermediate Level Attack. They investigate the mechanisms behind the resulting gains and combine the adapted methods. Their experiments report improved adversarial prompt generation without an obvious increase in computational cost.

For Llama-2-7B-Chat on AdvBench, 87% of the generated query-specific suffixes produce an exact match to the target output string. Separately, the reported attack success rates rise from 38% to 68% for query-specific prompts and from 26.68% to 60.32% for universal prompts compared with GCG. These results concern the named evaluation setting and distinguish exact target matching from the broader attack-success measure.
neurips-2024-improved-generation-of-adve.tldr: Adapting ideas from image attacks improves gradient-based adversarial prompt generation in the reported Llama-2-7B-Chat evaluation.

paragraphs: Image relighting predicts how a photographed scene would appear under different illumination. One approach first reconstructs explicit geometry and selected intrinsic scene properties, then uses a renderer to generate the new image. The paper identifies difficulties with controlling errors in this process and with representing effects beyond the chosen set of intrinsic properties.

The proposed method learns relighting directly from data. It represents both lighting and intrinsic scene properties as latent variables, so the representation of those properties is learned rather than supplied as an explicit set for rendering. This makes relighting the task through which the internal scene representation develops.

The authors report state-of-the-art relighting results for real scenes according to standard metrics. They also show that albedo can be recovered from the learned intrinsic representation without training on example albedos, with results competitive with state-of-the-art methods. This finding matters because training for relighting produces a representation from which a separate intrinsic property can be extracted, even without examples of that property.
neurips-2024-latent-intrinsics-emerge-fr.tldr: A data-driven relighting model learns latent scene properties that also support competitive albedo recovery without example albedos.

paragraphs: The paper studies drawing a new category after seeing just one example, a task humans can perform readily. Recent diffusion models have narrowed the performance gap, but the learning biases that make this possible have not been systematically examined. The authors focus on how those biases shape the internal representation used by latent diffusion models.

They compare several ways to regularize that representation. These include standard KL and vector-quantization regularization, supervised objectives based on classification and prototypes, and contrastive approaches using SimCLR and redundancy reduction. Comparing these choices makes the organization of the latent space a central experimental variable in the one-shot drawing task.

Models using redundancy reduction or prototype-based regularization produce drawings described as nearly human-like in both recognizability and originality. Psychophysical evaluation also finds that they better reflect human perception. The authors interpret these results as suggesting that the human-machine gap in one-shot drawing is almost closed. That conclusion concerns the studied drawing task and the perceptual qualities evaluated.
neurips-2024-latent-representation-matte.tldr: Redundancy reduction and prototype-based latent regularization produce nearly human-like one-shot drawings on the evaluated perceptual criteria.

paragraphs: Cross-domain few-shot segmentation transfers a model trained on a large source dataset to pixel-level labeling in a target domain with little data. Differences between the domains can sharply reduce performance. The paper begins with the observation that filtering different frequency components for target domains can improve results, sometimes by as much as 14% mIoU.

The authors attribute these improvements to lower correlations between feature-map channels. In their analysis, reduced correlation helps the model handle domain differences and activates larger regions for segmentation. They use this finding to design a lightweight frequency masker containing an Amplitude-Phase Masker and an Adaptive Channel Phase Attention module, both aimed at further reducing channel correlations.

The Amplitude-Phase Masker adds only 0.01% parameters and delivers an average performance improvement exceeding 10%. The attention module adds 2.5% parameters and brings a further improvement exceeding 1.5%. The reported results surpass existing state-of-the-art cross-domain few-shot segmentation methods, connecting a specific feature-level explanation with a compact architectural intervention.
neurips-2024-lightweight-frequency-maske.tldr: A lightweight frequency masker reduces feature-channel correlations and improves few-shot segmentation across domains in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: The paper studies optimization when different nodes in a communication network each hold part of a shared objective. The goal is to minimize the sum of their convex functions through decentralized computation and communication. Its focus combines two difficulties: the functions can be nonsmooth, and the network's communication links can change over time.

For settings with smooth functions or fixed network links, earlier work had established limits on the required computation and communication, together with algorithms meeting those limits. The combination examined here lacked both kinds of results. The authors establish lower bounds on the number of decentralized communications and subgradient computations needed to solve the problem.

They then develop an algorithm that matches those lower bounds, making it optimal in the complexity measures studied. Its theoretical performance substantially improves on the prior state of the art. Establishing both the bounds and a matching algorithm explains how much work the setting requires and shows that the proposed procedure reaches that limit within the analyzed framework.
neurips-2024-lower-bounds-and-optimal-al.tldr: The paper establishes computation and communication lower bounds for nonsmooth decentralized convex optimization on changing networks and provides a matching optimal algorithm.

paragraphs: LucidAction is a dataset for assessing how well an athletic action is performed. The paper argues that datasets drawn from individual competitions and limited to a single modality constrain both the breadth and generalizability of action-quality models. It introduces systematic collection organized around curriculum learning, so the data covers a progression of athletic skills.

The dataset has a three-tier hierarchy encompassing eight sports events and four curriculum levels. It includes RGB videos from multiple viewpoints as well as two-dimensional and three-dimensional pose sequences. A high-precision multi-view motion-capture system records complex movements, and annotations incorporate detailed penalties supplied by professional gymnasts to provide fine-grained assessment information.

The authors evaluate several contrastive regression baselines to investigate the challenges presented by the dataset. Ablation studies examine the benefits of multiple data modalities and detailed annotations for action-quality assessment. The contribution is therefore both a structured resource for studying skill quality and an experimental examination of which information can help models assess that quality.
neurips-2024-lucidaction-a-hierarchical-.tldr: LucidAction combines curriculum-structured sports performances, multiple camera views, pose data, and expert penalties for action-quality assessment.

paragraphs: The paper considers repeatedly choosing a set of at most k items from n possibilities when its value is initially unknown. The value function is monotone and submodular, meaning additional items provide diminishing returns. After each choice, the learner observes the set's value corrupted by mean-zero sub-Gaussian noise, creating a tradeoff between learning and collecting reward.

Performance is measured by regret relative to an approximation obtained through robust greedy maximization. The authors establish the first minimax lower bound for this setting, describing unavoidable regret in the worst case. They also prove a stronger lower bound for a slightly restricted class of algorithms, distinguishing the general problem from that more specific class.

Their Sub-UCB algorithm achieves an upper bound that matches the restricted-class lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Its guarantee minimizes an expression over L, combining a term proportional to L n^(1/3) T^(2/3) with a term involving the number of subsets of size k−L. The matching result establishes near-optimality for the restricted class, while the general lower bound remains distinct.
neurips-2024-nearly-minimax-optimal-subm.tldr: Sub-UCB nearly matches a new worst-case regret lower bound for a restricted algorithm class in noisy submodular set selection.

paragraphs: PCoTTA studies how a point-cloud model can adapt during use as its target domain keeps changing. The setting combines continual test-time adaptation with multiple tasks handled by one unified model. This creates a need to respond to new data while preserving useful knowledge and limiting the accumulation of errors during adaptation.

The framework uses three components. Automatic prototype mixture combines source prototypes with learnable prototypes using a similarity-balancing factor, aiming to prevent catastrophic forgetting. Gaussian Splatted feature shifting moves testing samples toward the source domain to mitigate online error accumulation. Contrastive prototype repulsion brings the nearest learnable prototype closer to a testing feature and separates it from other prototypes.

These components address complementary aspects of adaptation: retaining source information, reducing mismatch with incoming data, and keeping the evolving prototypes distinguishable. Experimental comparisons establish a new benchmark and show improved transferability to continually changing target domains. The paper's central contribution is a unified multi-task adaptation framework whose representation updates explicitly address both forgetting and error accumulation.
neurips-2024-pcotta-continual-test-time-.tldr: PCoTTA combines prototype mixing, feature shifting, and prototype separation to improve continual adaptation of multi-task point-cloud models.

paragraphs: The paper investigates adversarial vulnerability in pretrained vision-language models such as CLIP. Although these models can perform tasks without task-specific examples, adversarial perturbations can disrupt their predictions. The authors observe that such perturbations also shift text-guided attention, motivating an approach that explicitly constrains where the model attends.

Their framework, TGA-ZSR, uses two modules. Attention Refinement aligns the target model's attention on adversarial examples with the original model's attention on clean examples. The Attention-based Model Constraint compares attention from the target and original models when both receive clean inputs. Together, these mechanisms aim to improve robustness while preserving clean-input performance and generalization.

Experiments across 16 datasets report a 9.58% enhancement in zero-shot robust accuracy over the compared state-of-the-art techniques. The result supports text-guided attention as a useful intervention point for adversarial robustness. The two-module design matters because it addresses the perturbed-input behavior alongside the model's behavior on ordinary inputs, keeping both objectives within the same framework.
neurips-2024-text-guided-attention-is-al.tldr: TGA-ZSR constrains text-guided attention on clean and adversarial inputs, improving reported zero-shot robust accuracy across 16 datasets.

paragraphs: This paper asks how transformer expressiveness changes when inputs are sequences of numbers or numerical tuples rather than strings from a bounded token vocabulary. The distinction matters for data such as time series, where possible numerical values need not be restricted in advance. The authors study this question for Unique Hard Attention Transformers, or UHAT.

Their results show that UHAT on numerical data sequences can exceed the circuit class AC0 even without positional encodings, while remaining within TC0 even when positional encodings are included. These are theoretical bounds on expressive power. They establish that changing the input setting changes which computational properties this transformer formalism can represent.

The contrast also appears in language recognition. On strings, UHAT without positional encodings capture only regular languages; on data sequences, they can capture nonregular properties. The authors additionally show that UHAT capture languages expressible in an extension of linear temporal logic with unary numeric predicates and arithmetic. These results connect numerical-sequence processing to both circuit complexity and a logical description of expressible properties.
neurips-2024-the-power-of-hard-attention.tldr: Unique Hard Attention Transformers gain expressive power on numerical sequences, exceeding AC0 while remaining within TC0 under the stated settings.

paragraphs: UnlearnCanvas addresses how to evaluate attempts to remove unwanted generative capabilities from diffusion models. Such unlearning is motivated by concerns including harmful content and copyright disputes. The paper argues that existing evaluation systems can produce incomplete or inaccurate assessments, making it difficult to understand how well different unlearning methods work.

The authors introduce a high-resolution stylized image dataset supporting evaluation of artistic-style unlearning and associated objects. It enables a standardized, automated framework with seven quantitative metrics covering different aspects of performance. Using this framework, the paper benchmarks nine state-of-the-art diffusion-model unlearning methods and examines their strengths, weaknesses, and underlying mechanisms.

The study also investigates harder evaluation conditions: adversarial prompts that probe worst-case performance, removal of finer-scale concepts, and sequential unlearning. These settings broaden evaluation beyond a single removal task under ordinary prompts. The contribution is an assessment resource and comparative study intended to help develop more effective and robust unlearning methods, with the dataset, benchmark, and code made publicly available.
neurips-2024-unlearncanvas-stylized-imag.tldr: UnlearnCanvas supplies stylized images and a seven-metric framework for comparing diffusion-model unlearning methods under ordinary and challenging conditions.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether language models reason about causality or mainly draw on causal knowledge stored during training. The authors distinguish shallow, knowledge-driven level-1 reasoning from human-like level-2 reasoning. They argue that the evidence favors the former and analyze why the autoregressive mechanism of transformer language models is not inherently causal.

To test this interpretation, they introduce CausalProbe 2024, a causal question-answering benchmark containing material that is fresh and nearly unseen by the studied models. Performance drops substantially compared with earlier benchmarks. The authors interpret this as evidence that familiar causal knowledge plays a major role in the apparent reasoning abilities measured by existing evaluations.

They then propose G²-Reasoner, which incorporates general knowledge and goal-oriented prompts into the reasoning process. Experiments report significant improvements, especially in fresh and fictitious contexts. The work therefore combines a challenge to claims of human-like causal reasoning with a method intended to move beyond shallow reasoning; the reported improvements are presented as progress toward that goal.
neurips-2024-unveiling-causal-reasoning-.tldr: A fresh causal benchmark challenges claims of human-like LLM reasoning, while knowledge- and goal-guided prompting improves the evaluated models' performance.
